title: Finite locally constant set sheaves are coherent and stable under finite operations
statement: Let $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a Grothendieck topos [def-trf-coherent-topos] presented by a small finite-limit site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention] whose topology is generated by finite covering families. Call a sheaf of sets $F$ on $\mathcal E$ finite locally constant if there is a finite covering family $(U_i\to 1)$ of the final object and, for each $i$, an isomorphism on the slice topos $\mathcal E/U_i$ from $F|_{U_i}$ to the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on a finite set $M_i$. Every finite locally constant sheaf is a coherent object. Finite coproducts and finite limits of finite locally constant sheaves are finite locally constant. The image of any morphism between finite locally constant sheaves is finite locally constant, and if $R\rightrightarrows F$ is an internal equivalence relation with both $R$ and $F$ finite locally constant, then the quotient sheaf $F/R$ is finite locally constant.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Section 093P (section-locally-constant): Definition 093Q (definition-locally-constant), Lemma 093R (lemma-pullback-locally-constant), Lemma 093S (lemma-morphism-locally-constant) (1), Lemma 093U (lemma-kernel-finite-locally-constant) (1), finite limits and finite colimits of finite locally constant sheaves of sets on any site (images and quotients being coequalizers); coherence terminology from the Orgogozo §8.1 criterion.

proof.text: The finite-cover site criterion [lem-trf-finitary-site-coherent-generators] makes $\mathcal E$ coherent, makes every $H_V=h_V^\#$ ($V\in\mathcal C$) coherent, and makes every finite limit of such objects coherent; in particular the final object $1=H_{*}$ ($*$ the final object of $\mathcal C$) is coherent, hence quasi-compact [def-trf-coherent-topos]. Let $(U_i\to1)_{i\in I}$ be a finite trivializing family for $F$, the $U_i$ arbitrary objects of $\mathcal E$. The $H_V$ generate, so each $U_i$ receives an epimorphism from a coproduct of objects $H_V$; the composite family of all these $H_V\to U_i\to1$ is epimorphic onto the quasi-compact $1$, so a finite subfamily $(H_{V_k}\to1)_{k\in K}$ is epimorphic, each $H_{V_k}$ mapping through some $U_{i(k)}$. Pulling the trivialization $F\times U_{i(k)}\simeq\coprod_{M_{i(k)}}U_{i(k)}$ back along $H_{V_k}\to U_{i(k)}$ gives $F\times H_{V_k}\simeq\coprod_{M_{i(k)}}H_{V_k}$ (constant sheaf on a finite set $M$ in a slice $\mathcal E/W$ is $\coprod_MW$, as sheafification is a left adjoint and so preserves coproducts). So we may and do assume $U_k=H_{V_k}$, $k\in K$, coherent objects. Finite coproducts of coherent objects are coherent by [lem-trf-coherent-object-approximation].

source.place: Section 093P, Definition 093Q and Lemmas 093R, 093S, 093U; finite-cover coherence criterion in Orgogozo author draft §8.1

proof.text: Throughout, for an object $W$ of $\mathcal E$ the functor $-\times W$ preserves all colimits, epimorphisms and images: colimits in $\mathcal E$ are sheafifications of sectionwise presheaf colimits, sectionwise $-\times W$ commutes with colimits of presheaves of sets, and sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] commutes with finite products [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact] and fixes $W$, so $(\operatorname{colim}^{\mathrm{psh}}G_k)^\#\times W\simeq(\operatorname{colim}^{\mathrm{psh}}(G_k\times W))^\#$. With the representable trivializing family $(U_k=H_{V_k})_{k\in K}$ of Step 1 and trivializations $F\times U_k\simeq\coprod_{m\in M_k}U_k$, each $m\in M_k$ gives a section $s_{k,m}:U_k\to F$, and $p:P=\coprod_{k}\coprod_{m\in M_k}U_k\to F$ is an epimorphism: $\coprod_kU_k\to1$ is an epimorphism, hence so is $\coprod_k(F\times U_k)\to F$, and each $F\times U_k$ is the image of the summands indexed by $M_k$. $P$ is coherent by Step 1. Its kernel pair is the finite coproduct $R=P\times_FP=\coprod_{(k,m),(l,n)}E_{km,ln}$, where $E_{km,ln}\hookrightarrow U_k\times U_l$ is the equalizer of $s_{k,m}\mathrm{pr}_1$ and $s_{l,n}\mathrm{pr}_2$. Fix one such pair and put $W_j=U_k\times U_l\times U_j=H_{V_k\times V_l\times V_j}$ ($j\in K$), coherent by Step 1; the $W_j\to U_k\times U_l$ form a finite epimorphic family. On $W_j$ the two sections become maps $W_j\to F\times W_j\simeq\coprod_{a\in M_j}W_j$ over $W_j$; by finite extensivity [lem-trf-set-sheaf-finite-extensivity] they decompose $W_j=\coprod_aW_{j,a}=\coprod_aW'_{j,a}$ (pullbacks of the summands), and the equalizer restricted to $W_j$ is $E\times_{U_k\times U_l}W_j\simeq\coprod_a(W_{j,a}\times_{W_j}W'_{j,a})$, a coproduct summand of $W_j$ again by extensivity. A summand $S$ of a quasi-compact object $W=S\sqcup S'$ is quasi-compact: an epimorphic family onto $S$ together with $S'\to W$ is epimorphic onto $W$, a finite subfamily is, and pulling it back along $S\to W$ (disjointness and universality) leaves a finite epimorphic subfamily onto $S$. So each $E\times_{U_k\times U_l}W_j$ is quasi-compact; these finitely many objects cover $E$ (pullback of an epimorphic family along $E\to U_k\times U_l$), so $E$ is quasi-compact (refine any epimorphic family onto $E$ on each of them), and the finite coproduct $R$ is quasi-compact by the same argument [def-trf-coherent-topos]. The quotient criterion [lem-trf-coherent-epimorphic-quotient] applied to $p$ gives that $F$ is coherent.

source.place: Section 093P, Lemmas 093S and 093U(1), with the finite-cover presentation argument of Orgogozo author draft §8.1

proof.text: For a finite family of finite locally constant sheaves, the products $U_{i_1}\times\dots\times U_{i_r}$ of members of their trivializing families form a common finite trivializing family (an epimorphism stays one after $-\times W$, Step 2), and on each member every sheaf of the family is $\coprod_{M}W$ for a finite set $M$. A morphism $\coprod_MW\to\coprod_NW$ over $W$ decomposes, by finite extensivity [lem-trf-set-sheaf-finite-extensivity] applied to the finitely many maps $W\to\coprod_NW$, along a finite decomposition $W=\coprod_cW_c$ into summands on each of which it is $\coprod_MW_c\to\coprod_NW_c$ induced by a map of finite sets; replacing $W$ by the $W_c$ keeps a finite epimorphic family of $1$. Finite limits and coproducts commute with $-\times W_c$ (limits by construction of the slice, coproducts by Step 2 [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact]), so on each member the terminal object, products, equalizers and finite coproducts are $\coprod_LW_c$ for the corresponding finite set $L$ (one point, product, equalizer, disjoint union). This proves closure under finite limits and finite coproducts, the empty cases being the constant sheaves on one point and on $\emptyset$.

source.place: Section 093P, Lemma 093S(1), together with the finite-limit and finite-colimit argument for finite locally constant sheaves

proof.text: Given $\varphi:F\to G$ between finite locally constant sheaves, take the finite refinement of Step 3, on each member $W$ of which $\varphi\times W$ is $\coprod_MW\to\coprod_NW$ induced by a map of finite sets $f:M\to N$. Images commute with $-\times W$ (an image is the equalizer of the cokernel pair, and $-\times W$ preserves pushouts by Step 2 and finite limits), and the image of $\coprod_MW\to\coprod_NW$ is the summand $\coprod_{f(M)}W$: the inclusion of a summand is monic [lem-trf-set-sheaf-finite-extensivity] and $\coprod_MW\to\coprod_{f(M)}W$ is split epi on each summand. So $\operatorname{im}(\varphi)\times W\simeq\coprod_{f(M)}W$ on each of finitely many members, and the image is finite locally constant.

source.place: Section 093P, Lemma 093S(1), morphism and image closure for finite locally constant sheaves

proof.text: Let $R\rightrightarrows F$ be an internal equivalence relation with $R$ and $F$ finite locally constant. Take the finite refinement of Step 3 for both projections; on each member $W$ they are $\coprod_NW\rightrightarrows\coprod_MW$ induced by maps of finite sets $a,b:N\to M$. The quotient $F/R$ is the coequalizer of $R\rightrightarrows F$, and $-\times W$ preserves coequalizers (Step 2), so $(F/R)\times W$ is the coequalizer of $\coprod_NW\rightrightarrows\coprod_MW$, which is $\coprod_{Q}W$ with $Q$ the coequalizer of $a,b$ in finite sets (a coequalizer of a map of coproducts of the single object $W$ is computed on index sets, since $\coprod_{(-)}W$ is a left adjoint from sets to $\mathcal E/W$). $Q$ is finite, so $F/R$ is finite locally constant. This is the finite quotient argument behind Stacks 093S(1), with no infinitary operation.
